item.title: 美国在联合国会议上退出法国，抗议盟友对美国人权记录的批评
item.description:
联合国（美联社）——周一，在美国的欧洲亲密盟友批评特朗普政府的人权记录后，法国外交官在联合国发表讲话时，美国外交官纷纷离场。
联合国安理会就乌克兰问题举行会议期间采取了这一令人惊讶的举动，此前美国反对向联合国提供援助。人权事务高级专员沃尔克·图尔卡诺尔 (Volker Türkanother) 任期四年。周五的连任得到了压倒性的支持，其中包括来自法国的支持。
美国的罢工不仅反映出美国总统特朗普与法国总统马克龙之间的紧张关系，也反映出美国和欧洲之间更广泛的紧张局势。这些问题包括特朗普对北约的承诺、美国可能做出的改变等问题。在欧洲的军队部署，以及特朗普想要控制属于北约成员国丹麦的格陵兰岛。
特朗普抱怨说，没有征求欧洲人的意见，他们在伊朗战争期间没有向美国提供帮助。在紧张局势中，马克龙带头努力建设欧洲军队，并确保与英国一起成为欧洲大陆两个核大国之一的核保护伞。
周一短暂罢工后，美国副大使丹·内格里亚指责法国假装“道德愤怒”，假装就包括人权在内的每个话题向世界说教。
他说，美国在每一次“自由受到威胁”的冲突中都与法国站在一起，并“出于友情和相互尊重”容忍法国的哗众取宠，但仅此而已。
引发罢工的原因是法国驻日内瓦联合国代表团周五在社交媒体上发帖，批评美国反对联合国人权事务负责人连任。大会以 144 票对 10 票、13 票弃权支持蒂尔克，其中美国投了“反对”票。
“美国曾经是人权的灯塔。现在不再是了。今天，它与朝鲜、尼加拉瓜、马里和俄罗斯并肩而立，被孤立。世界不再听它的，”法国代表团在推特上写道。
美国驻联合国大使迈克·沃尔兹（Mike Waltz）在 X 台上做出回应，指责法国纵容“一些最严重的侵犯人权者”，并投票给“那些一直在向美国、英国和以色列等自由、主权民主国家说教，同时又巴结世界上最严重的压迫者的人”。
蒂尔克作为联合国人权事务负责人的工作本质上是很棘手的：它需要公开反对该世界组织成员国政府的侵犯人权行为。
例如，图尔克尖锐批评俄罗斯 2022 年入侵乌克兰和以色列在加沙的战争，并敦促在世界杯之前“大规模重新思考”美国的移民政策，理由是围绕“种族定性、监视和移民执法”的问题。
在周一的会议上，内格里亚谈到了法国。
“今天，我提醒他们，美国仍然是世界自由的灯塔，”他说。“因此，在他们放弃居高临下和不尊重的言论并以与其在安理会席位相称的方式行事之前，我们不会为他们提供政治化胡言乱语的好处。”
当法国驻联合国大使杰罗姆·博纳丰在安理会会议结束时被要求发言回应时，他从未提及罢工事件。
相反，他指出帮助美国获得独立的法国参加了 7 月 4 日美国成立 250 周年的庆祝活动。
“联合国成立的目标是致力于国际和平与安全、人权和发展，”他说。“所有这些构成了法国在联合国内工作的精神……维护这个机构、它的独立性、它为《宪章》服务以及为人权与和平服务的能力。”

item.title: 日本南部九州岛发生7.1级地震，数十人受伤或失踪
item.description:
东京（美联社）——官员称，日本南部主岛九州周二发生7.1级地震，一座购物中心的部分设施和一家造纸厂的巨大烟囱倒塌，造成数十人受伤或失踪。发出了Atsunami警告，但很快就解除了。
人们担心至少有两人死亡。
据熊本县首府消防部门称，在鹿岛镇，地震导致永旺梦乐城购物中心二楼倒塌，被困人数不详。
熊本县应急小组表示，四人受伤并被送往医院，另有 10 人下落不明。声明称，随着搜救工作的继续，损失程度仍在调查中。
熊本应急小组表示，日本造纸工业公司八代工厂的烟囱倒塌，建筑物受损，11 人被困在废墟下。研究小组表示，其中两人后来被发现没有生命体征，而另外九人的情况不明。
消防和灾害管理局表示，建议超过 26 万人撤离，其中大部分在熊本县，但也有邻近的长崎县。
受影响地区位于该国首都东京西南约 900 公里（540 英里）处。
日本气象厅表示，熊本县西海岸和三个邻近县的有明海和八代海的海啸警报在两小时内解除。
日本首相高市早苗告诉记者，有报道称道路、桥梁和建筑物遭到破坏，以及停电和火灾，但细节尚不清楚。
美联社记者查尔斯·德莱德斯马报道称，日本南部部分地区发生强烈地震，引发海啸警报。
消防厅表示，主要公共设施或基础设施没有受损。日本原子能监管机构表示，附近三座核电站没有发现异常情况。
共同社称，八代市的一家医院收治了约 40 名伤者，另有约 50 人被送往熊本市的一家医院。
此次地震还影响了九州多家主要制造商。
丰田汽车公司表示，出于安全问题，该公司已暂停九州三座工厂的运营，并将于周三重新开业。丰田表示，目前还没有人员受伤或工厂受损的报告，但该公司仍在评估情况。
据《日经新闻》报道，本田汽车公司和日本制纸公司也暂停运营，大和运输公司也停止了进出熊本的送货服务。
根据机场网站上的通知，九州的新干线子弹头列车和当地列车被暂停以进行安全检查，阿苏熊本机场的跑道也被关闭，“短期内不可能恢复运营”。没有详细信息。
日本防卫省表示，已派遣军用飞机前往该地区评估局势。
共同社称，一列火车在八代车站脱轨并侧翻，熊本城的石墙也被损坏。熊本城是主要的旅游目的地，在 2016 年的地震中受损严重，目前仍在修复中。
“晃动让我想起了熊本地震（10 年前），我很害怕，”三船町政府官员下田弘树 (Hiroki Shimoda) 说，他看到附近房屋的屋顶瓦片倒在地上。2016 年，熊本遭受了一场致命地震，造成至少 50 人死亡。
日本气象厅的清本真司敦促居民在未来两到三天内保持谨慎。
美联社驻东京撰稿人影山尤里对此报道也有贡献。

item.title: 特朗普与内塔尼亚胡自发动伊朗战争以来首次会面
item.description:
WASHINGTON (AP) — Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and President Donald Trump met at the White House on Tuesday for the first time since they launched a joint war against Iran, offering a chance for Netanyahu to smooth out strains in their relationship.
The closed-door meeting lasted nearly an hour and a half and was “positive and productive,” according to White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt. The White House did not immediately offer more details.
Despite signs of tension between the two ahead of the sitdown, Netanyahu was effusive afterward and called it “excellent” in a post on his Instagram profile.
“When I say excellent, I don’t mean it in a superficial way,” Netanyahu said in Hebrew. “A conversation with full partnership, with mutual support, with an understanding of the common goal of ensuring that Iran does not have nuclear weapons, and other goals as well. One of the best conversations I’ve had with the President of the United States, our friend Donald Trump.”
It comes as both face growing pressures at home. Netanyahu is up for reelection and is embattled in part because of his deteriorating relationship with Trump. Trump is under pressure to end anunpopular warthat haswreaked economic havocanddriven prices higherahead of midterm elections this November.
Trump revealed some tension with Netanyahu ahead of their meeting, complaining about reports that the Israeli leader plans to discuss intelligence on Iranian activities atPickaxe Mountain, a potential nuclear site that the U.S. president has threatened repeatedly to bomb.
“I know exactly what’s going on at Pickaxe,” Trump told “Fox & Friends.” He insisted that whatever Iran is doing is “not a big problem” and that “Bibi’s telling me that because he wants me to stay involved.”
“Why do you have to announce to the world?” Trump added, flashing his frustrations with his ally.
Near the White House where the public was able to gather near fencing, a small group of protesters chanted, “Netanyahu, you’re a tyrant” and “Bibi, you’re not welcome here,” referencing the prime minister’s nickname.
The two leaders also planned to discuss the framework agreement the U.S. and Israel signed with Lebanon over the Israel-Hezbollah war and the expansion of the Abraham Accords, according to a White House official, who spoke on condition of anonymity to preview the meeting.
“We have a little difference,” Trump said Monday when asked by reporters if he and Netanyahu were on the same page on Iran. “But pretty close, yeah.”
Trump has had ahot-and-cold history with Netanyahuover the years, but upon his return to the White House last year, their alliance seemed stronger than ever. When they started the war together in February, it was with a united front, touting their respective militaries as acting in lockstep to take out Iran’s leadership and pave the way for a government more friendly to the West.
But as Iran fought back — sending drones and missiles slamming into U.S. bases and high-rises in cities in the Gulf, and choking off the Strait of Hormuz — Trump came under immense pressure both at home and by allies in the region to end the conflict.
Since then, Netanyahu, who wanted to continue the fighting in Iran and against its ally, Hezbollah, in Lebanon, has been sidelined as Trump sought a deal with Tehran. His visit to the White House this week comes as the disagreements with Trump and Vice President JD Vance have burst into the open over the war in Iran and more.
“The Americans are making it clear to the Israelis they are the ones who are running the war,” Israeli journalist and political analyst Amit Segal wrote Monday in the daily newspaper, Israel Hayom. “It is clear to everyone that Israel has been put in the back seat.”
With U.S.-Iran tensions flaring again in recent weeks, Netanyahu planned to share with Trump Israeli intelligence on Tehran’s nuclear program, according to a person familiar with Netanyahu’s visit, who spoke on the condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak to the media.
Israel’s United Nations Ambassador Danny Danon told reporters in New York on Tuesday that Netanyahu wants to hear what Trump would like to see over the coming days and weeks.
“I cannot tell you which direction it will go. There are different options,” he said. “We are prepared for all scenarios, and we will discuss it with the president.”
Netanyahu said Sunday that he hoped to sit down with Trump “to hear what he has in mind” for Iran.
“Because I think, in many ways, it’s his decision” on how to move forward, Netanyahu told Maria Bartiromo on Fox News Channel’s “Sunday Morning Futures.” “If he can do so without returning to intense military fighting, that’s fine. Why not?
“But one way or the other, they have to end their nuclear program,” he said of Iran.
But even as Netanyahu sees an opportunity, he also needs to persuade Trump that he won’t play spoiler to U.S. diplomatic and reconstruction efforts in Gaza and in Lebanon, where the president has previously complained that “too many people are being killed” by Israeli strikes.
Israel has taken recent steps in both places.
In Lebanon, where the Israeli military occupies much of the south, Israel agreed to allow the Lebanese army to deploy to some villages as part of a “pilot program” testing their ability to secure areas where Hezbollah once operated. The U.S. State Department said Monday that the next round of talks between Israel and Lebanon will take place next week in Rome with a focus on expanding the program.
On Gaza, Israel’s security cabinet green-lit on Sunday a measure that would, in theory, grant entry to the first members of an international stabilization force outlined last year in a U.S.-backed ceasefire deal between Israel and Hamas.
Few countries have pledged troops for the force, however, and Israel would approve their entry into Gaza on a case-by-case basis.
The troops — including from Morocco and Uganda — would only be allowed to operate in a small, desolate area in Rafah in the south, where the plan is to vet and house some displaced Palestinians.
The Israeli military continues to carry out strikes it says target militants but that have also killed civilians.
Israel has lost a significant amount of bipartisansupport in the United States, particularly over its conduct in Gaza.
In June, Vance warned Israeli officials that Trump was their only friend among world leaders. Vance is expected to attend the meeting with Netanyahu, according to a person familiar with the plan who was not authorized to speak publicly and spoke on condition of anonymity.
AnAP-NORC pollpublished earlier this month found a dramatic erosion of support among American adults for Israel.
“We’ve lost America. Thank you, Bibi,” wrote Ben Caspit, a political commentator for Israel’s Maariv newspaper.
Associated Press writers Melanie Lidman in Tel Aviv, Israel, Darlene Superville and Seung Min Kim in Washington, Edith M. Lederer at the United Nations and Bill Barrow in Atlanta contributed to this report. Cunningham reported from Jerusalem.

item.title: 威斯康星州龙卷风造成广泛破坏并导致数千户家庭断电
item.description:
MADISON, Wis. (AP) — A tornado struck northeastern Wisconsin on Monday, blackening the midday sky and sending workers sheltering in office basements as fierce winds splintered homes, scattered twisted metal across a highway and knocked out power to more than 30,000 people.
There were no reports of fatalities or injuries as of Monday evening, but emergency officials were still searching, said Gordon Hintz, Winnebago County’s top elected official.
The National Weather Service confirmed a tornado in Winnebago County, about 90 miles (145 kilometers) northwest of Milwaukee. Damage was reported in cities including Appleton and Menasha, where Police Chief Matt Albrecht said some homes and businesses were “severely impacted.”
The twister was spun off by a large storm system that moved through the Great Lakes, fueled by a buildup of heat and humidity, National Weather Service meteorologist Scott Berschback said.
Hintz said it could be several days before power in the stricken area is restored.
People walk among debris after a tornado struck Monday, July 27, 2026, in Menasha, Wis. (AP Photo/Kayla Wolf)
Heather Schroeder said she heard cracking and popping all around her as the tornado tore apart a laundromat, a bakery and a neighborhood tavern that were clustered around a street corner in Menasha, about 30 miles (50 kilometers) south of Green Bay.
Rescue workers pulled someone out of one of the buildings, said Schroeder, who works nearby. She said it wasn’t clear if the person had survived. Cars were turned upside-down, and there was a gas leak at the laundromat, she said.
The twister ripped roofs off homes and flipped vehicles in one neighborhood in Menasha, just blocks from the shores of Lake Winnebago. Video showed a trail of destruction, with some homes reduced to their outer walls.
Greg Van Driest was working in downtown Appleton when the sky got as dark as night.
“The word we all were using was ‘ominous,’” he said. “It’s like, ‘Whoa, look at that.’ ... You looked outside and you thought it was three in the morning, it was that dark.”
Cassandra Baron, left, and Brooke Baron pull fallen tree branches off of a car after a tornado struck Monday, July 27, 2026, in Menasha, Wis. (AP Photo/Kayla Wolf)
Hintz said he’s received multiple reports of buildings destroyed and vehicles overturned. All storm warnings that could be made ahead of time to get people to safety were activated, he said.
“Obviously when you look at the damage, Mother Nature doesn’t really care,” he said.
Weather service meteorologist Holley Kamba said the agency was receiving reports of damage in southern Outagamie County and eastern Winnebago County,
“We have been receiving calls of damage with a lot of trees down, power lines down,” Kamba said. “We’ve been searching for some pictures of the structural damage.”
Wisconsin Gov. Tony Evers said the state “is ready to assist communities however we can.”
Weather service meteorologists in Green Bay issued a tornado warning at 11:59 a.m. for the Fox Cities region, which includes Appleton, Menasha and Neenah. It warned of flying and dangerous debris, damage to mobile homes, vehicles and trees, while warning people to seek shelter.
The area had already been under a severe thunderstorm warning for about 45 minutes, and meteorologists indicated the storm was capable of producing winds up to 60 mph (97 kph).
An upside down car sits in front of a damaged bakery after a tornado struck Monday, July 27, 2026, in Menasha, Wis. (AP Photo/Kayla Wolf)
Images on social media showed extensive damage in Appleton, including homes stripped of roofs, a car tossed onto a lawn, and streets littered with tree limbs.
The Appleton Police Departmentsaid on social mediathat it was aware of “several downed trees and large tree limbs throughout the city.” Traffic signals were out and some roads were “heavily backed up,” the department said.
Outagamie County Executive Tom Nelson said he didn’t have any confirmation of fatalities or injuries in the county, which includes Appleton. But he said there was “extensive and severe damage” in Menasha and Fox Crossing.
“All indications are that this was a devastating system that has caused extensive damage,” Nelson said.
In Menasha, the electric utility said the entire city of about 18,000 people was believed without power. Authorities were opening a shelter at a church.
The storm hit Menasha and the east side of neighboring Fox Crossing at around 12:20 p.m., Albrecht said.
Debris is seen in front of a damaged house after a tornado struck Monday, July 27, 2026, in Menasha, Wis. (AP Photo/Kayla Wolf)
“At this point, we are unaware, unsure of how bad the damage is because many roads in those same areas are impassable,” Albrecht said, adding emergency crews were seeking to enter the affected area to “look for injuries, look for victims” and clear the roads.
He urged people to stay away from the hard-hit areas: “Right now, there are many downed power lines, downed trees, multiple hazardous situations. Please stay out.”
Later Monday the storm was clearing out of Wisconsin and moving south of Milwaukee through the Chicago area as it began to dissipate, he said.
Mayes-Osterman reported from Chicago and Seewer from Toledo, Ohio. Christopher L. Keller in Albuquerque, New Mexico; Laura Turbay in Little Rock, Arkansas; Sophie Bates in Jackson, Mississippi; Hannah Schoenbaum in Salt Lake City; and Michael R. Sisak in New York contributed to this report.

item.title: 捕鲸博物馆因“有史以来最糟糕的水族馆”T恤、手提包而走红
item.description:
New Bedford is considered the home of whaling’s history in America — and now, home to the worst aquarium ever.
In 2020, a Google user left aone-star reviewof the New Bedford Whaling Museum coining that phrase. Last fall, the museum began selling shirts and hoodies with the review on the back and a whale skeleton on the front. Now, the design is capturing national attention.
On Wednesday night, theCBS Evening Newsran a segment about the merchandise afterWPRI, Providence’s CBS affiliate, covered the story Tuesday. Sales are booming.
Overnight, a slew of buyers rushed to get their hands on the merch, seemingly proud to represent such an accolade.
Customers placed 738 online orders, mostly for “worst aquarium” merchandise, between the broadcast Wednesday night and 2:30 p.m. Thursday afternoon, according to Annelise Conway, the chief engagement officer at the Whaling Museum. On Thursday, orders for the week were up 250% compared to the week prior.
Amanda McMullen, president and CEO of the New Bedford Whaling Museum, said the review has been folklore among the staff for a while, always providing “a good chuckle.” In 2020, there was no aquarium at the museum. What it lacked in live aquaculture, it makes up forin skeletons, including those of a 66-foot blue whale, a 37-foot humpback whale, a 49-foot North Atlantic right whale, and a 48-foot sperm whale — all in all, a few more bones than guests typically want to see in an aquarium.
Emily Roznoy, the designer of the merchandise and the visitor experience manager at the Whaling Museum, said she had heard staff jokes about putting the infamous review on a T-shirt. When she saw a barbecue restaurant selling shirts that contained a similarly condemning review (one star, “no vegan options”), she made the design a reality. The review appears on the back of T-shirts, crewneck sweaters, and tote bags; a drawing of the museum’s sperm whale skeleton adorns the front.
“I knew the humor was there,” McMullen said, recalling her first reaction to the design. “And I got the sense that New Bedford has this fighting spirit of place.”
Who could resist repping an honor like this one?
Conway said this week’s attention started with an advertisement via anInstagram postannouncing the restock of the design on T-shirts and crewnecks last week. Prior to that, a TikTok video showcasing the merchandise in November got more than 96,000 views.
Even before virality, the design was a hit, consistently ranking in the top five of the store’s sales, Conway said. Before the ad ran last week, the store was running low and ordered a resupply of 160 more adult T-shirts — already more than they usually put in for.
The morning after the CBS segment, Roznoy called to update the order with an additional 750 adult T-shirts, 400 youth size T-shirts, 750 crewnecks, 400 hoodies and 150 tote bags, with the prospect of coffee mugs on the horizon.Online, each adult shirt sells for $32.50, with crewnecks costing $50 and hoodies $60. The tote bag sells for $39.95.
On Thursday morning, the store on the Whaling Museum’s first floor was swimming with enthusiasm.
“Do you know if they will be ordering more of these?” a guest asked, pointing to the crewneck hanging on the wall. An employee nodded.
Another staff member answered the phone and said, “they are on back order right now, but you can still purchase it online,” seemingly responding to an inquiry about the viral design.
A customer purchased a crewneck, and the cashier smiled, saying, “You’re one of the cool kids now.”
Cyn Spence from Dartmouth was one of the “cool kids” that morning, purchasing a crewneck and tote bag as surprise gifts for a friend leaving the area.
“It’s just perfect,” Spence said of the merchandise. Her sister-in-law had sent her a video of the merchandise, and she said she knew she had to come get it. She described the design as “genius.”
McMullen said the witty design helps to support the Whaling Museum’s approach to marketing itself as a fun and interactive museum, backed by serious scholarship.
“I’m just honestly, above all else, proud of them for running with it,” McMullen said. “They took a chance on something, and it obviously hit.”
Timing adds irony to the design. The review was posted when the museum was more a whale ossuary than an aquarium. But early this year, the Whaling Museum installed an exhibit that features a 250-gallon saltwater tank, or what McMullen described as “a modest aquarium.” The tank, in the middle of the first floor, houses local South Coast species including the blue crab, Forbes’ sea star, and northern puffer fish. (Yet no live whales — much to the one-star reviewer’s continued disappointment, one could imagine.)
The tank was installed as a partnership with UMass Dartmouth’s School for Marine Science and Technology. Museum officials said the tank is important to the discussion of the South Coast’s ecology and coastal water health.
Conway said the museum has been receiving feedback that the design reflects a hearty New England and Massachusetts spirit.
“There isn’t a strategy to be authentic,” Conway said. “It just sort of happens.” The design is a product of a “very local” staff, she said. ”The person who sold you your ticket is the person who is modeling the merchandise.”
Roznoy grew up in Rochester, Massachusetts, and has lived in New Bedford for half a decade. When the line first launched last fall, she said she and her team expected mostly staff to be interested in it. The national audience is exciting and surprising, she said.
“I have always wanted to be an artist and graphic designer,” Roznoy said. “So knowing I made something people really like makes me really happy.”
Conway and Roznoy both said the design was a way to connect with a broader audience at the Whaling Museum.
“We aren’t a ‘shhh’ museum,” Conway said. “We don’t want to be exclusive. … We want to interact with the community, not stand behind glass.”
This story was originally published byThe New Bedford Lightand distributed through a partnership with The Associated Press.

item.title: 佛罗里达州因谋杀女孩而判处前警官死刑，单日将执行两起处决中的第一起
item.description:
STARKE, Fla. (AP) — A former police officer convicted of the on-duty rape and murder of a young girl was put to death Tuesday, the first oftwo lethal injectionsplanned for a single day in Florida, hours before an 80-year-old man was to become the second-oldest inmate executed in modern U.S. history.
Tuesday marked the first time since two convicted murderers were executed on a single day — in Arkansas in 2017 — that a state has planned virtually back-to-back executions. It also comes 18 months after Republican Gov. Ron DeSantis began stepping up executions at a pace unseen in Florida since the U.S. death penalty was reinstated in 1976, making his the busiest death chamber in the nation.
Since the beginning of 2025, Florida has carried out nearly half the state executions in the U.S.
James Aren Duckett, 68, was pronounced dead at 1:19 p.m. following a three-drug injection at Florida State Prison near Starke. The 11th inmate executed by the state this year, Duckett was convicted of raping and drowning an 11-year-old girl while working as a police officer in a small central Florida city in 1987.
Duckett declined to make a final statement, responding “no sir” when asked. About 4 minutes after the execution began, the prison’s warden shook Duckett and shouted his name, but there was no response.
Later Tuesday, barring any last-minute development, 80-year-old Dominick Anthony Occhicone was scheduled to become the oldest prisoner executed in Florida’s modern history starting at 6 p.m. Occhicone was convicted of killing his ex-girlfriend’s parents in 1986.
Until Tuesday, a total of 17 executions had been carried out in the U.S. so far this year, with Florida leading the way with more executions than all other states combined.
Both men had made last-ditch appeals to the U.S. Supreme Court, and last week, the Florida Supreme Court denied appeals by both men to intervene.
Duckett’s attorneys had unsuccessfully claimed Duckett’s innocence and argued the state’s handling of the DNA evidence is the reason for the inconclusive results.
Occhicone’s attorneys had argued that several age-related ailments, including kidney and prostate problems, could make his execution especially painful, constituting cruel and unusual punishment.
DeSantis hasn’t said why he scheduled two executions six hours apart. A Florida prison official said Tuesday morning that the department was confident in its readiness to carry out both executions. All Florida executions are by injection of a sedative, a paralytic and a drug that stops the heart, according to the Department of Corrections.
DeSantis, who leaves office in January, oversawa record 19 executions in 2025, more in a single year than any other Florida governor since the reinstatement of the death penalty in the U.S. in 1976. The previous high waseight executionsset in 2014.
Florida has executed 29 people since the beginning of 2025 while the rest of the U.S. states combined have carried out 35 executions over the same time frame.
If the day’s final execution is carried out Tuesday evening, that would bring total executions for DeSantis’ final two years in office to 31 overall, compared to just nine executions during his first six years in office. With another execution set for August, 2026 could also be a record-breaking year.
Nationwide, it’s not uncommon for two different states to hold executions on the same date, but it’s less common for a single state to perform two in a day. Before Florida, Arkansas last executed two inmates on the same day by lethal injection three hours apartin April 2017. And Texas executed two convicted killers on the same day in 2000, the year the state executed40 prisoners.
Floridians for Alternatives to the Death Penalty urged DeSantis ahead of Tuesday to halt both executions.
“July 28 represents an unprecedented escalation of Florida’s use of the death penalty,” the group’s executive director, Grace Hanna, said in a statement. “These are two profoundly different cases, but they point to the same troubling reality: Florida continues to expand the use of capital punishment, despite mounting evidence that it is not what Floridians want.”
DeSantis has rarely commented on the pace of executions, but previously said that his goal is to bring justice to victims’ families who have waited decades for death sentences to be carried out.
“Some of these crimes were committed in the ’80s,” the governor said last year. “Justice delayed is justice denied. I felt I owed it to them to make sure this ran very smoothly. If I honestly thought someone was innocent, I would not pull the trigger.”
If his execution proceeds as planned, Occhicone would become thestate’s oldest inmateto be executed just weeks after two 74-year-old men briefly held that spot, the second man just a week older than the first at his time of death.
Occhicone also would become the second-oldest prisoner known to be put to death in modern U.S. history after83-year-old Walter Moody Jr.was executed in Alabama in 2018 for a wave of southern mail bombs in 1989 that killed a federal judge and wounded a Black civil rights attorney.
DeSantis initially signed a death warrant for Duckett in February, scheduling his execution for March 31. But the Florida Supreme Court issued a stay just days before the planned execution to allow for DNA testing of old evidence that couldn’t be performed at the time of the original trial because of technological limitations. The results came back inconclusive, meaning that they did not exonerate Duckett or definitively connect him to the crime. Judges have allowed the jury verdict to stand.
When Occhicone’s death warrant was signed late last month, his was the only execution scheduled for Tuesday. But after the Florida Supreme Court removed Duckett’s stay on July 8,DeSantis signed a new deathwarrant on July 14 and added Duckett to Occhicone’s execution date, which hadn’t been done in Florida in more than 60 years.Florida Department of Corrections recordsshow multiple executions on a single day were more common in the past, with the last being on May 12, 1964.

item.title: 特朗普政府敦促最高法院在中期选举前允许针对邮寄投票的命令
item.description:
华盛顿（美联社）——特朗普政府周一要求最高法院为唐纳德·特朗普总统的一项行政命令扫清道路，该命令可能会在 11 月中期选举之前极大地改变邮寄投票方式。
司法部要求法官们暂停下级法院的裁决，阻止全国近一半地区的彻底变革。
这一请求是在特朗普发表黄金时段讲话后不久提出的，该讲话加强了他多年来对选举合法性提出质疑的努力，这可能是高风险中期选举之前法庭面临的几个与投票相关的挑战之一。
特朗普三月份命令政府创建一份合格选民的“州公民名单”，并只向名单上的人邮寄选票。
23个州和哥伦比亚特区的民主党官员提起诉讼，称宪法赋予各州和国会制定选举规则的权力，而不是总统。他们的律师表示，特朗普提议的改革已经成熟，很容易被滥用，并可能造成混乱。
马萨诸塞州的一名法官阻止了原告州的行政命令，美国第一巡回上诉法院的分歧小组在周末维持了她的裁决。
该行政命令要求美国公民和移民服务局以及社会保障管理局专员向州官员发送联邦公民名单，以确定合格的选民。它告诉美国邮政服务只向名单上的人邮寄选票。
该命令还要求选票使用带有独特条形码的安全信封以供追踪。不遵守规定的州和地方可能会被扣留联邦资金。
上诉称，特朗普的命令列出了“一般政策指导”，并不直接规定各州如何进行选举。副检察长约翰·绍尔 (D. John Sauer) 要求高等法院在诉讼进行时冻结法官的命令，称其站不住脚。
绍尔写道：“该禁令尤其站不住脚，因为各机构仍在考虑如何（如果有的话）执行该命令，但地方法院先发制人地裁定，无论各机构可能选择做什么，都必然是非法的。”
他敦促高等法院迅速采取行动，认为任何新政策都必须尽快在 8 月出台，才能在 11 月的选举中生效。对上诉的答复将于 8 月 3 日到期。
邮寄投票长期以来一直是特朗普最喜欢的目标，甚至他也曾使用这种方法自己投票。他将自己在 2020 年输给民主党人乔·拜登的责任归咎于此，并在没有证据的情况下声称这为欺诈打开了大门。周一，他在密歇根州通用汽车工厂露面时又回到了这个主题，当时他正在呼吁国会通过他的选民身份证和公民身份证明法案。
“希望不会有邮寄选票，”他说，并称这些选票“本质上是腐败的”。
联邦数据显示，邮寄选票越来越受到两党选民的欢迎，在 2024 年总统选举期间，大约有 30% 的选票是通过邮寄方式投出的。该过程也是安全的。布鲁金斯学会 2025 年的一项研究发现，每 1000 万张邮寄选票中只有大约 4 起欺诈案件。
最高法院此前曾就邮寄选票做出不利于特朗普政府的裁决，并于 6 月份裁定各州可以清点选举日之后送达的选票。
特朗普在其行政命令中提出了拟议的修改，作为阻止非美国公民投票的保障措施。他还多次敦促通过需要公民身份证明才能投票的立法。
非公民投票已被证明是罕见的，并且是一种重罪，可能会被驱逐出境。
由民主党总统巴拉克·奥巴马提名的波士顿美国地方法院法官英迪拉·塔尔瓦尼于 6 月同意停止执行 11 月 3 日的选举。
她的裁决与华盛顿另一位联邦法官的裁决不同。特朗普任命的美国地区法官卡尔·尼科尔斯在五月份发现，阻止该命令还为时过早，因为该命令尚未实施。
负责各州诉讼的加州总检察长罗布·邦塔办公室没有立即对特朗普政府的上诉发表评论。纽约总检察长利蒂西亚·詹姆斯办公室拒绝置评。
邮政局也不会以正在进行的诉讼为由，讨论其有关执行特朗普命令或其规则的计划。在堪萨斯州，共和党国务卿斯科特·施瓦布的办公室表示，尚未收到邮政局关于未来计划的消息。
美联社驻堪萨斯州托皮卡的记者约翰·汉纳 (John Hanna) 对这篇报道做出了贡献。

item.title: 前奥运选手被控破坏倒影池，认为大陪审团程序存在“违规行为”
item.description:
华盛顿（美联社）——一名前奥运会选手被控故意破坏林肯纪念堂倒影，普利斯寻求获得导致他被起诉的所有闭门证词，指出大陪审团程序中存在“违规行为”。
在周一提交的法庭文件中，大卫·赫恩的律师请求命令政府交出所有大陪审团诉讼的完整记录。他们还希望检察官披露他们向大陪审团提供的有关赫恩涉嫌犯罪要素的法律指示。
赫恩本月早些时候对一项破坏财产重罪罪名表示不认罪，并计划于 9 月 28 日在华盛顿特区高等法院开始审判。该指控指控赫恩对泳池造成至少 1,000 美元的损坏，一旦定罪，最高可判处 10 年监禁。
但他的律师质疑检察官是否向大陪审团提供了足够的证据来支持赫恩起诉书中指控的损害数额。辩护律师称，一名国家公园管理局官员作证说，在赫恩涉嫌触碰泳池之前，该泳池就已经遭到损坏，无法量化赫恩造成的任何损坏，并表示无论他的行为如何，都需要进行同样的修复。
“证人的证词证实，在赫恩先生做出任何指控的行为之前，泳池已经存在严重损坏，需要修复，”他的律师写道。“据目击者称，泳池每周泄漏的水超过一百万加仑；其伸缩缝已超过使用寿命；内衬已出现裂口。”
赫恩的律师将这些论点建立在他们对大陪审团证词的有限审查之上。他们希望法院下令了解所有诉讼程序。
美国检察官珍妮·皮罗华盛顿办公室的发言人没有立即回复寻求对赫恩的论点发表评论的电子邮件。
赫恩此前要求法院驳回此案，该案源于唐纳德·特朗普总统倡导的耗资数百万美元的翻修项目，陷入困境。他的律师辩称，政府未能妥善保存倒影池中的重要物证。
共和党人特朗普声称有人破坏了泳池，但政府批评者将问题归咎于维修工作质量低劣。特朗普周一在密歇根州通用汽车公司发表讲话时声称，一名“病人”割破了泳池内的衬垫，但表示该景点正在接受治疗。
特朗普说：“现在正在医院里，但很快就会好起来。”“快要开业了。”
赫恩和他的支持者声称，对他的起诉是特朗普政府出于政治动机试图转移责任并寻找替罪羊。
赫恩特告诉美联社，6月19日，他在骑自行车时停在泳池边，随后被国民警卫队和美国公园警察拘留了五个小时。他说，他伸手检查泳池新剥落的涂层，并短暂触摸了附着在泳池一侧的一块块，但他说，他服从了一名公园工作人员的要求，让他放开它。
美国奥林匹克和残奥委员会在其网站上称，67 岁的赫恩来自马里兰州贝塞斯达，参加了三届夏季奥运会，并在 1996 年亚特兰大奥运会上获得了第九名。
同一法庭至少还有另外三人因涉嫌从泳池中清除油漆而被指控犯有轻罪。
___ 美联社撰稿人 Darlene Superville 对本报告做出了贡献。

item.title: 民主党初选导致党内分裂，共和党人谴责美国民主社会主义者的新政纲
item.description:
纽约（美联社）——最近取得几场初选胜利的进步团体的一个新纲领正在成为共和党攻击的素材，因为共和党希望在 11 月中期选举之前将民主党人描绘成极端主义者和共产主义者。
尽管美国民主社会主义者的工人应得更多平台不一定与候选人自己的议程完全一致，但知名共和党人周末对此予以谴责。DSA纲领提议起草“新宪法”，对美国政府结构进行重大改变，包括废除参议院、用国会选出的领导人取代总统和最高法院以及允许所有美国永久居民投票。除了这些变化之外，本月早些时候发布的该平台还呼吁进行一系列社会改革。
“野蛮人已经进了大门——民主党人正在欢迎他们进来，”众议院议长、路易斯安那州共和党人迈克·约翰逊在 X 上写道。“共产主义不再是一个牵强的威胁。它就在我们的海岸上！”
《华尔街日报》的保守派编辑委员会也对这一议程发出警告，称其激进，并写道，共和党人和愿意的民主党人的工作是让全国了解这一议程。但它警告共和党人避免共产主义攻击路线，称它们不会引起年轻一代的共鸣。
在全国范围内参加民主党初选的进步派和 DSA 支持的候选人并不都同意该组织的完整议程。左翼也分为进步派和温和派，他们对于推动民主党前进的最佳政策有不同的想法。但 DSA 平台为共和党人提供了一个大范围攻击民主党人的机会，因为他们在竞选中寻求优势，从而决定明年哪个政党在国会中获得多数席位。
唐纳德·特朗普总统今年又恢复了称民主党为共产主义者的老习惯，称他们想要“摧毁美国传统的生活方式”。其他共和党人也纷纷效仿，在心怀不满的美国人对外国战争和高生活成本感到愤怒之际，他们花了几个月的时间捍卫自己的政党，转向更舒适的领域。
DSA 7 月中旬提出的国家愿景提出了重大变革，该组织表示，这些变革可以部分在现行体系下实现，但最终需要“从头开始建设一个新社会”。
建议的改革包括扩大投票权、公开资助所有选举、用多党民主取代两党制度、建立大公司公有制、扩大移民权利，同时结束移民和海关执法局的拘留和驱逐出境。
该组织联合主席梅根·罗默最近在“福克斯周日新闻”节目中确认了议程的各个方面，同时承认其中一些提案，例如废除边界和监狱，将被视为长期计划的一部分。
共和党全国委员会周末在一篇帖子中呼吁人们关注该平台，几名共和党议员抓住这一机会发出警报。
“这些人疯了，”得克萨斯州参议员特德·克鲁兹 (Ted Cruz) 在 X 上回复道。
“仔细观看这段视频，”众议院第二号共和党众议员史蒂夫·斯卡利斯写道。“这些想法可能会比你想象的更早进入你的社区。”
DSA 的议程是在一致的候选人在最近的几场民主党初选中取得胜利的情况下提出的。他们利用选民对政党建制派的愤怒以及对美国与以色列联盟日益增长的怀疑，在纽约和科罗拉多州的众议院竞选中击败温和派。
民主社会主义候选人也在华盛顿特区、纽约和西雅图等美国主要城市的市长选举中取得成功。即将到来的密苏里州初选将由 DSA 支持的前国会女议员与温和的民主党现任议员对决，这将进一步考验该运动的势头。
在其他选举中，进步候选人概述了他们与 DSA 议程的不同之处。例如，在即将举行的密歇根州参议院初选中，进步候选人阿卜杜勒·赛义德与社会主义保持了距离，称他相信资本主义，但需要对其进行监管。
与此同时，包括前民主党全国委员会主席海梅·哈里森在内的建制派民主党人强力反击参加党内初选的 DSA 候选人，同时批评该党的行事方式。
“我这么说并没有恶意或敌意：如果你讨厌民主党，那么请不要竞选我们的提名，”哈里森在六月的社交媒体帖子中写道。“不要使用我们的资源。不要依赖我们的志愿者。不要使用我们的基础设施。不要要求民主党人在你的竞选活动中投入时间、金钱和精力。专注于建设你真正支持的政党。”

item.title: 国际足联计划斥资 200 亿美元运营世界杯，这遭到了欧洲欧足联的愤怒
item.description:
GENEVA (AP) — FIFA President Gianni Infantino’s plan to create a $20 billion company running theWorld Cupwith private investors including the Kushner family was announced Tuesday — and immediately attacked by European soccer body UEFA.
“It is not FIFA’s to sell,” UEFA said in a statement. “None of us are the owners of football.”
Infantino’s plans to form a commercial subsidiary, which would be called FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), running competitions like the World Cup andClub World Cupwas first reported by The Times of London.
FIFA said in a statement FFE would raise up to $4.2 billion later this year to help fund development programs “based on an initial equity valuation of $20 billion by carefully selecting long-term investors who will purchase minority, non-controlling interests.”
FIFA is working with J.P. Morgan while intended investors include Thrive Eternal launched by Joshua Kushner, whose brotherJared Kushneris a son-in-law ofU.S. President Donald Trump.
The men’s World Cup that finished this month only deepened thepolitical and personal ties between Trump and Infantino, andfueled concerns about those tiesincludingfrom UEFA.
“The soul and governance of football are not assets to trade — especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially,” UEFA said Tuesday, responding to the reports of selling stakes in FIFA competitions.
FIFA is currently a Swiss-based not-for-profit association of its 211 national member federations worldwide.
Those members must approve any plan and would get the chance “to access up to $20 million in one-off capital,” FIFA said.
“This is about the democratization of football worldwide,” Infantino said in a FIFA statement, which added that “a consultation process has begun.”
UEFA, however, said it took reports of the project “extremely seriously. So should every national Football Association.”
“This crosses a line that football’s governing institutions should never cross,” said UEFA, which comprises 55 of the FIFA members.
The outline of Tuesday’s surprise announcement was, FIFA said, detailed by Infantino to members who met in Manhattan on July 18 ahead of the World Cup final. There, Infantino promised to “unleash the commercial potential and opportunity that FIFA has.”
FIFA’s statement Tuesday about its proposed project led on how much money each of its 211 members could get through 2038 in the “FIFA Fast-Forward Program.”
Instead of the currently promised $8 million each in development funds through the 2027-30 World Cup commercial cycle, it would be $20 million, then $22 million and $24 million in the following cycles.
FIFA banked record World Cup income of about $12 billion from the 2026 tournament which hadunprecedented high prices for ticketsand hospitality across the U.S., Canada and Mexico. It already was unclear how that money could be matched from Spain, Portugal and Morocco co-hosting the 2030 men’s edition.
Member federations could choose if they wanted to take part in the new financial opportunities, FIFA said.
“FIFA would retain sole control of FFE and exclusive authority over football governance, competitions, match calendar, and all regulatory and sporting decisions,” the soccer body said.
FIFA’s integrity standards werecalled into questionduring the World Cup, including byteam coaches,Norway’s soccer federationand a top European public body, the Council of Europe.
The project announced Tuesday is the second time in Infantino’s increasingly controversial 11-year presidency he has tried to push through a multi-billion dollar deal with private backers.
In 2018,Infantino proposed a secretive $25 billion offerover 12 years with SoftBank of Japan to create new global competitions, including an expanded men’s Club World Cup, seemingly backed by Saudi Arabian money.
That ultimately failed after meeting fierce resistance from UEFA, which saw threats to its prize assets: the Champions League and the European Championship.
Infantino still built closer ties to Saudi soccer and the kingdom’sCrown Prince Mohammed Bin Salman.Saudi Arabia will host the 2034 World Cupand largely funded the revamped men’s Club World Cup hosted in the U.S. last year.
The financial success of the just-ended World Cup has looked likely to ensure Infantino is re-elected next year unopposed for a fourth and final term in office through 2031.
At hisre-election by acclaim in 2023in Rwanda, Infantino suggested any CEO delivering similar financial results would be kept in the job forever.
Speculation has swirled for years Infantino might want a different global role in soccer beyond his FIFA presidency, which is due to end when he is 61.
The Times reported Tuesday that a CEO-like commissioner role of the new FFE operation could be created for Infantino.
“This has never been discussed,” FIFA said in a statement Tuesday. “However, the FIFA president and the FIFA administration will and must have leading roles in this entity — if approved.”
There was no timetable suggested Tuesday for debate and decisions by FIFA, its ruling Council chaired by Infantino, and the 211 members.
FIFA is scheduled to hold an online congress on Nov. 23 to confirm hosts of the Women’s World Cup editions in2031 and 2035.

item.title: 规则小组表示，在世界杯四分之一决赛对阵阿根廷的比赛中将瑞士球员罚下场是错误的
item.description:
日内瓦（美联社）——足球立法小组澄清了其对裁判的指导意见，确认瑞士前锋布雷尔·恩博洛不应在世界杯四分之一决赛对阵阿根廷的比赛中被罚下场。
第72分钟，瑞士将比分追成1-1平后，恩博洛在视频回放后因模拟犯规而吃到第二张黄牌，改变了比赛的势头。
阿根廷队在加时赛中以 3-1 获胜，红牌判罚引发了包括前对手埃及在内的抱怨，裁判的判罚偏向梅西的球队。
国际足联支持的规则小组（IFAB）周一发表澄清称，针对“身份错误”案件的 VAR 协议不适用于世界杯上的此类事件，尽管在未来的比赛中可能会出现这种情况。
总部位于苏黎世的国际联合会在一份声明中表示：“然而，在审查结束之前，它可能不会被这样使用。”
恩博洛在受到阿根廷中场球员莱昂德罗·帕雷德斯的挑衅时倒地，后者被出示黄牌。
VAR官员提醒裁判，帕雷德斯并没有犯规，相反，恩博洛被出示了第二张黄牌，并被罚下场。
这并不是目前“错误身份”的应用方式，即当向没有犯下最初受罚犯规的错误球员出示牌时纠正裁判。
“裁判做出了错误的决定，”瑞士队主教练穆拉特·亚金在堪萨斯城比赛结束后说道。“我知道他们会保护他们的裁判，但这条规则毁了我们今天的比赛，这非常痛苦，以这种方式被淘汰也很痛苦。”
国际足联澄清说，这张卡“只能通过审查来确定犯下被处罚罪行的球员；罪行本身不能被审查/改变。”
自三月份以来，对 VAR 协议的审查一直在进行，IFAB 承认像恩博洛这样的事件是其中的一部分。
“在 2026 年 FIFA 世界杯期间使用错误身份条款来处理模拟问题受到了好评，”这家总部位于苏黎世的组织表示。
IFAB 由国际足联任命的官员和四个英国足球联合会组成。其年度会议于每年二月或三月举行，以更新在重大赛事或下一赛季生效的比赛规则。
周二，欧足联称赞国际足协的明确性是“值得欢迎的解释”，欧足联已接待了来自 55 个成员联合会的裁判老板，以重新制定新赛季的决策原则。
欧足联强调：“VAR 并不是要重新裁判比赛。”并表示需要更短的视频回顾和更轻松的干预。
在经历了令人沮丧的视频评论赛季（尤其是英超联赛）之后，国际足联针对世界杯的整体 VAR 策略受到了赞扬。
欧足联表示：“冗长、微观的审查往往是一种症状，表明场上的决定并不明确且明显错误，因此应该受到限制。”并制定了“当裁判的决定明显错误或裁判错过了明显事件时”的干预标准。
欧足联还鼓励国际足联在三月份同意并由国际足联在世界杯上强制执行，打击比赛中浪费时间的行为。
欧足联表示：“将指示裁判严格一致地执行新规则。”
欧足联本赛季将组织男子和女子俱乐部比赛，包括欧洲冠军联赛、男子国家联赛的国家队比赛、2028年欧洲杯预选赛以及2027年女子世界杯预选赛。

item.title: 情绪激动的齐达内在执掌法国队时实现了他的“梦想”
item.description:
PARIS (AP) — Moments after being announced as France’s new coach on Tuesday, Zinedine Zidane clenched his fists and his usually measured voice trembled a little.
“I’m excited,” he said. “The France team makes you dream. We have extraordinary players, an extraordinary team.”
Zidane coached Real Madrid until leaving in 2021. He replacesDidier Deschampsat the helm of France team he led to glory as arguably its greatest ever player.
“I’ve waited five years for this chance, so that’s why I’m a bit emotional,” said Zidane, adding that it was the happiest day of his career as coach.
“I’ve always watched this side as a fan and also as a future coach, I won’t hide it.” Zidane added. “That’s why I didn’t take a club side. I told myself that the only thing I wanted to do after Madrid was taking the France team.”
French Football Federation president Philippe Diallo announced Zidane’s appointment at the FFF headquarters in Paris on Tuesday, saying he has been given a 4-year contract.
Diallo called the hiring of Zidane “an exceptional moment,” calling Zidane “one of the legends of French soccer.”
The 54-year-old Zidane could have gone to another club after leaving Madrid in 2021. But there was no way he would.
“I had some offers during the five years I was away to take charge of a club,” he said. “I turned them all down for the France team. It was the only thing I wanted to do.”
Zidane called it “an immense joy” taking charge.
“I have so many emotions,” he said. “I am ready for the challenge.”
Zidane praisedDeschamps, who won the 2018 World Cup and stepped down after the recent edition, where Les Bleuslost in the semifinalsto Spain.
“I will give everything so that this team can win,” Zidane said. “I would also like to congratulate DD (Deschamps) for these remarkable years.”
Diallo said he met Zidane for talks in February, 2025 after Deschamps said he would stand down following the 2026 World Cup. Zidane said France would play differently to how it did under Deschamps.
“What motivates me is the game, I was a No. 10, I like goals,” Zidane said. “I was a leader on the field and now I want to be a leader by experience.”
His first game will be away to Turkey in the Nations League on Sept. 25, followed by a match in Belgium three days later.
Home fans need to wait until Oct. 2 for a glimpse of Zidane at Stade de France, when France plays Italy, 20 years after he was sent off against Italy in the 2006 World Cup final for headbutting Italy defender Marco Materazzi.
“I’ve noted all of the four matches to come,” Zidane said, tapping his forehead. “Italy is special, because I played there, because I know people, because I speak Italian. All of those things.”
After the announcement, Zidane greeted a large gathering of fans outside the federation headquarters and they cheered loudly when he arrived.
France lost the World Cup final on penaltiesin 2022and lost the European Championship final on home soil in 2016. Some Deschamps critics, among them former France teammate Christophe Dugarry, said he should have won more with the players he had.
Deschamps described an “an unbreathable atmosphere” at the end of his tenure, without detailing what the tensions were.
Zidane and Deschamps were different types of midfielders, but are forever linked by glory.
The industrious Deschamps was France’s captain and the mercurial Zinedine was the creative force when France won the 1998 World Cup and Euro 2000.
Affectionately nicknamed “Zizou” his face was beamed onto the Arc de Triomphe the night France celebrated its first World Cup triumph in ’98. An inspired Zidane scored two headers in the final in a 3-0 win against Brazil at Stade de France and later that year he won the Ballon d’Or.
Born in Marseille to Algerian parents, Zidane grew up playing in the estate of La Castellane, which has a giant mural of Zidane on one its tower blocks. It was on the estate’s concrete pitches where Zidane nurtured his incredible balance, to avoid falling on the rock-hard ground.
Zidane’s club career took him from Cannes to Bordeaux and then to two of the world’s biggest clubs: Italian giant Juventus and Madrid.
His international career began in 1994, when he scored two stunning goals against the Czech Republic after coming on as a substitute, in front of his home fans in Bordeaux.
He won league titles with Juve and Madrid and scored a brilliant volley to help Madrid win the Champions League in 2002.
With Zidane carrying an injury, France flopped at the 2002 World Cup — going out in the group stage — but reached the 2006 final after Zidane came out of international retirement.
His performance in a 1-0 victory over Brazil in the quarterfinals was Zidane at his balletic best: a hypnotic combination of drag-backs, stepovers, spins on the ball, and flicks over the shoulder.
The Brazilians were in awe and even Ronaldinho — a Ballon d’Or winner himself — seemed captivated.
His 108th and final game for France was against Italy in the final and he scored early with a deft Panenka-style penalty for his 31st, and last, international goal.
Then, with millions watching around the world, an infamous moment saw him walk back up the field and slam his forehead into Materazzi’s chest, sending the tall defender flying backward.
Zidane trudged past the gold-tinted World Cup trophy as he left the field in Berlin, his international career over.
Now he has another chance to lead Les Bleus to glory.

item.title: 法官裁定歌手 D4vd 必须因杀害 14 岁塞莱斯特·里瓦斯·埃尔南德斯而受审
item.description:
LOS ANGELES (AP) — A judge ruled Monday that there is enough evidence to putD4vdon trial in the killing and dismemberment of 14-year-oldCeleste Rivas Hernandez, who authorities said had threatened to expose their relationship and crater the indie-pop singer’s rising career just a few days before his debut album dropped.
“i will end ur career and ur life,” she told him in a text message sent the night before her death.
Los AngelesJudge Charlaine Olmedodecided that evidence presented during a preliminary hearing provided probable cause for a trial on charges of murder, continuous sexual abuse of a child under 14 and unlawful mutilation of human remains.
The dark and disturbing details presented over five days brought tears, gasps and horror to the courtroom. The evidence included grisly autopsy photos, explicit descriptions and depictions of sexual abuse and a stark picture of the final texts she sent minutes before she died and her phone went permanently silent.
The ruling was a major step in the 10-month investigation and prosecution of D4vd that began when the dismembered and decomposing body of a girl was found in the trunk of his Tesla in the Hollywood Hills in September while he was on tour.
D4vd, the 21-year-old whose legal name is David Burke, showed no emotion when the judge issued her ruling, watching calmly and intently in his orange jail clothes and glasses as he had throughout the proceedings.
He haspleaded not guilty. His lawyers argued that the murder evidence was insufficient, but did not argue against the other two charges. They declined to comment outside court.
Prosecutors argued that the evidence was overwhelming.
“Based on the mountains of evidence presented,” Deputy District Attorney Beth Silverman said, “all of the allegations have been proved way beyond the standard required.”
Los Angeles District Attorney Nathan Hochman said outside court that prosecutors presented only a “small fraction” of the evidence they have. They are still weighing whether to seek the death penalty, but Burke is eligible for it after Olmedo also found probable cause for lying in wait, killing for financial gain and killing a potential witness, special circumstances in a crime that allow for a death sentence.
Olmedo ordered that Burke continue to be held without bail. An arraignment is to be held on Aug. 31, and a trial could happen as soon as 60 days later.
Before the decision, prosecutors gave a moment-by-moment account of Rivas Hernandez’s last night.
As she neared his Hollywood home shortly after 10 p.m. on April 23, 2025, in an Uber he had sent to pick her up, she sent her final text: “girly pop i’m almost there open ur door if ur home.”
Prosecutors allege Burkestabbed her to deathwhen she came through the door.
The night before, the two argued via text about his relationship with a woman. She sent him an angry and profanity-riddled text saying she will tell her dad so many lies about him and that she would “end ur career and ur life.” She had sent several similar messages around the same time.
Prosecutors said thatBurke met Rivas Hernandezwhen she was 11, began sexually abusing her when she was 13 and he was 18. A year before her death, the pair also exchanged messages about how she had become pregnant — she assured him the baby was his — and that she had an abortion.
During the preliminary hearing, prosecutors introduced photos of the two of them kissing and lying in bed. The pictures showed that she had “David” tattooed in red ink on a finger — one of two that had been cut off when her body was found.
Prosecutors said they have records showing Burkeordered chain sawsand wading pools that he used to dismember her body in his garage, and that her DNA was found there onblood stains.
They said he then drove around for weeks and even months with the body in his trunk before the seemingly abandoned Tesla wastowed from the Hollywood Hills.
The defense argued that the evidence didn’t show the kind of malice that was required for murder.
“There’s no evidence that Mr. Burke harbored a deliberate intent to kill Miss Hernandez,” said Burke’s attorney, Marilyn Bednarski.
She said the communications between Burke and Rivas Hernandez showed “no threat, no evidence of a history of violence” and that he had “the opposite of homicidal malice” toward her.
She argued that a medical examiner ruling that her death was a homicide from two puncture wounds was too vague and inconclusive to be evidence of murder. The defense did not directly give an alternative theory on how she died and isn’t required to.
The defense also established that she had asked seven times to come to see him in the days before her death, and he reluctantly agreed only after she demanded it, and that she had threatened to kill Burke and to mutilate him.
Silverman told the judge that “the defense tried numerous times throughout these proceedings to dirty up the victim” despite her being a child.
Farrell, the detective, also said under defense questioning that the parents of both Burke and Rivas Hernandez knew about their relationship, that he had attended church with members of her family and that her parents had given their consent for her to go to London with him for a week.
Patrick Steinfeld, an attorney for Rivas Hernandez’s family said after the hearing that they were “horrified that the defense attorneys brought up evidence to put the blame on a 14-year-old girl.”
Her parents sat in the front row through most of the hearing, but sat out some of the more graphic parts and left in the middle of the sexual testimony after her mother began crying.
D4vd(pronounced “David”) became an online musical phenomenon as a teen with a blend of indie rock, R&B and lo-fi pop. He had huge followings on TikTok, Soundcloud and Spotify, where his top songs, including his 2022 breakthrough “Romantic Homicide,” have more than a billion plays.
In 2024 he played the Coachella music festival and released his first full-length album, “Withered,” two days after authorities say Rivas Hernandez was killed.

item.title: 艺术家贝蒂耶·萨尔 (Betye Saar) 去世，享年 99 岁，其作品反映了黑人身份
item.description:
艺术家贝蒂耶·萨尔 (Betye Saar) 周日上午在洛杉矶去世，享年 99 岁，其作品反映了黑人身份、文化和精神。
萨尔的亲属周一证实了他的死讯。这周她就满100岁了。
作为 20 世纪 60 年代黑人艺术运动的核心人物，萨尔开创了组合盒或用现成物品制成的雕塑，并将吉姆·克劳时代的纪念品重新塑造为黑人解放的强大图腾。
“她的作品具有丰富的象征意义，随着时间的推移不断演变，以展示其存在的环境、文化、政治、种族、技术、经济和历史背景，”代表她的洛杉矶画廊 Roberts Projects 表示。
Saar 的职业生涯始于设计，并于 35 岁时转向艺术。直到 90 多岁，她仍继续创作艺术。她在帕萨迪纳长大，是附近阿尔塔迪纳黑人艺术家社区的一员。她经常引用西蒙·罗迪亚（Simon Rodia）的瓦茨塔（Watts Towers）作为早期的灵感来源。
萨尔的实践结合了绘画、版画、雕塑和发现的物品，包括娃娃、洗衣板和其他古董。船、钟表、笼子和祭坛在她的实践中反复出现，以及神秘学和宇宙学的象征。她经常以狮子的形式引用她的狮子座星座，并在许多作品中加以强调。
该画廊表示：“她对黑人收藏品、传家宝和实用物品的挪用是通过颠覆而改变的。”“在美国老一辈黑人艺术家中，萨尔是无可非议的。”
1969 年制作的《黑人女孩的窗户》具有开创性。尽管如此，直到几十年后，它才被广泛庆祝，并于 2019 年被纽约现代艺术博物馆收购。“当时洛杉矶没有那么多画廊，当然也没有黑人艺术家的画廊，”她曾在接受采访时表示。
1972年创作的《杰迈玛阿姨的解放》是她最重要的作品之一。它展示了她收集的诋毁黑人的纪念品，其中包括一位“妈妈”，即 19 世纪的吟游诗人角色，她在为白人奴隶主服务时微笑着。
但在萨尔的手中，这个人物又被重新利用：她微笑着，但拿着一支步枪和一枚手榴弹。
这是对 1968 年牧师遇刺事件的回应。田纳西州孟菲斯的马丁·路德·金。萨尔说金的死“引发了我内心的愤怒，神秘主义者变成了战士”。
“我对使用这些强有力的负面图像犹豫不决——思考白人如何看待黑人，以及这如何影响黑人看待彼此的方式，”萨尔说。“拯救它的是我把杰迈玛阿姨塑造成了一个革命人物。”
130 多年后，桂格燕麦公司宣布将于 2020 年退役其“Aunt Jemima”品牌，并承认该标志及其起源“基于种族刻板印象”。
萨尔教导和指导了几代黑人艺术家，包括画家克里·詹姆斯·马歇尔。
尽管萨尔的作品曾在 1975 年惠特尼美国艺术博物馆的个展中展出，但在接下来的几十年里，大型机构只偶尔展出她的作品。不过，2019 年，洛杉矶县艺术博物馆和 MoMA 同期举办了个展。
2026 年春天，萨尔入选美国艺术与文学学院。
“她对艺术创作有着无穷的精力。我认为她有很多话要说，并且厌倦了白人男性主导的艺术世界，”2023 年制作并导演了一部关于萨尔生活的纪录片的安吉拉·罗宾逊·威瑟斯彭 (Angela Robinson Witherspoon) 说道。《贝蒂耶·萨尔：准备成为一名战士》采访了约翰·传奇、蒂娜·诺尔斯和其他知名人士。
“她正在抚养三个年幼的女儿，她想成为民权运动的一部分，”罗宾逊·威瑟斯彭说。
专注于服装设计的“Let's Get It On：贝蒂·萨尔的穿着艺术”目前正在洛杉矶的 Robert Projects 展出，最终的 100 个娃娃中的 26 个将在曼哈顿的纽约历史协会展出。
本文首次发表于2026年7月27日。于2026年7月28日更新，更正了公司名称。这是桂格燕麦，而不是桂格燕麦。此外，曼哈顿纽约历史博物馆最终展出的 100 个娃娃中，只有 26 个，但数量不超过 100 个。
美联社撰稿人安娜·弗曼在洛杉矶提供报道。

item.title: Cracker Barrel 首席执行官在徽标失败一年后辞职
item.description:
Cracker Barrel 的首席执行官辞职近一年，此前该连锁店试图重塑品牌，但遭到了顾客的强烈反对。
Cracker Barrel 周一表示，首席执行官 Julie Masino 将于下个月辞职，但将以顾问身份继续留在公司直至 10 月 9 日。
David Deno 将于 8 月 10 日接替 Masino 担任首席执行官。Deno 从 2019 年起一直担任 Bloomin’ Brands 的首席执行官，该公司拥有 Outback Steakhouse 和其他连锁店，直至 2024 年退休。他还曾在百思买 (Best Buy) 和百胜餐饮集团 (Yum Brands)（肯德基和塔可钟的母公司）担任高管职务。
总部位于田纳西州黎巴嫩的 Cracker Barrel 于 2023 年 7 月聘请了长期担任 Taco Bell 和星巴克高管的 Masino。她因​​创新者的记录而被选中，希望她能为 Cracker Barrel 吸引新顾客，该公司在 43 个州经营着近 660 家餐厅。
Masino 推出了更新的菜单项，例如 Hashbrown Casserole Shepherd’s Pie，以增加 Cracker Barrel 的晚餐客流量。她还开始改造公司昏暗、充满古董的餐厅，减轻墙壁的重量并安装更舒适的座椅。
然后，去年八月，Cracker Barrel 宣布计划放弃其长期的标志，该标志的特点是一个年长的、穿着工作服的男人靠在一个木桶上，以及“Old Country Store”字样。该公司表示，将继续在其菜单和商店销售的商品上纪念赫歇尔叔叔（Uncle Herschel）——其标志中的男子代表 Cracker Barrel 创始人的叔叔。但新标志将更简单，更容易在路标和手机应用程序中阅读。
立即遭到强烈反对。粉丝们不喜欢新标志，也反对商店的重新设计。就连总统唐纳德·特朗普也加入进来，在《Truth Social》的一篇帖子中表示，Cracker Barrel“应该回到旧的标志，根据客户的反应（最终民意调查）承认错误，并比以往更好地管理公司。”
马西诺在几天内改变了方向，但损害已经造成。去年秋天，Cracker Barrel 的同店餐厅销售额下降了 5%，在截至 2026 年 1 月 30 日的季度中下降了 7%。与其餐厅相关的零售店的同店销售额进一步下降。
尽管如此，该公司的股东在 11 月投票决定让 Masino 继续担任首席执行官，而且近几个月销售趋势已开始改善。截至 5 月 1 日的季度，同店餐厅销售额下降 2.6%，该公司上调了全年收入和利润预测。
Masino 还通过出售公司的 Maple Street Biscuit Co. 商店，帮助加强了公司对 Cracker Barrel 品牌的关注。Cracker Barrel 于 2019 年收购了 Maple Street，并在全国各地经营 50 个门店。
花旗分析师乔恩·塔尔周一在一份研究报告中表示，考虑到最近的改善，马西诺离职的消息令人惊讶。
Cracker Barrel 股价在午后交易中下跌 2.7%。
